findings.title: Listed evidence file hash failures outside the two-name allowlist still certify a green run
findings.reachable_precondition: The real directory contains candidate.json/helper plus the helper's cache-worker-fixture.events or scenario file. A read of that listed evidence file fails during the final artifact scan while the two required rows and candidate/manifest links remain readable. This can be a later EIO after the GO event was already read.
findings.actual_call_path: runPositivePilot -> REAL_DEPENDENCIES.artifactFacts maps the failed file to digest:null,error:EIO with top-level error:null -> evidenceProblemsOf builds a map but inspects only REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS (candidate/helper). It ignores the errored events/scenario row -> judge sees no evidence problem -> normal ok/0 or fault-observed/1, authoritative=true. The legacy validator also only checks the same two names.
findings.contract: R5E SPEC B2 requires per-row full SHA/error gating; B3 makes mandatory evidence/hash unreliability exit3. The tool's own judge contract at1450 says every row, and its manifest presents these real event records as hashed run evidence rather than optional ignored errors.
findings.impact: An explicit failed evidence read remains in the manifest while producer/CLI and legacy consumer qualify the run. A later external checker might reject it, but the claimed repaired producer gate still permits false green. No orphan or malicious-native exploit is alleged.
findings.minimal_fix: Check error and /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ for every published artifact row, reject duplicate/invalid names and incomplete byte facts, separately require the two mandatory names. Alternatively explicitly exclude truly optional evidence before manifest creation under a MAIN contract change; do not silently certify an included errored row. Include these problems in judge before publishing.
findings.direct_counterexample_design: Under guarded actual runner/main and real temporary FS, create a real events file; at artifact-scan read only, inject EIO for its read through the fs boundary while leaving candidate/helper/manifest reads real. Require failed/faultfalse/authorityfalse/exit3 in both modes and actual persisted row error. Add malformed full-hash and duplicate-row controls at the private facts boundary. Do not execute a C/N or mutate frozen source for this review.
findings.test_gap: New tests1330-1389 cover only missing/error/mismatch of candidate/helper. They do not drive a real mapper error on a third listed evidence file.
findings.runtime: NOT_RUN; static branch counterexample, not a captured old-code failure

findings.title: The tool's joint validator never reads bytes, and consumer tests exercise a third copy rather than the actual consumer
findings.reachable_precondition: Publication returns successfully with non-null digests, then a required actual-file read fails or serialized file contents no longer satisfy the linked protocol. Current main never performs that read. A listed errored evidence row from O01 already provides an actual producer path to a bad manifest; helper evidence loss after publication is another checker counterexample.
findings.actual_call_path: main -> runPositivePilot -> publishEvidence returns hash of its serialized buffer -> jointQualification(outcome) checks only authoritative/published/protocol/equal internal exit/non-null hash strings. It has no root, fs reads, JSON parsing, byte lengths or content/link checks. It accepts ordinary failed/exit1 as accepted:true as well (main returning ordinary1 is allowed, but accepted:true must never mean expected-fault PASS). Legacy has a separate richer jointQualification; it reads three JSON records, but never reads/rehashes the required helper, accepts any string helper digest and ignores non-required row errors. The executable consumer test invokes its own consumerAccepts copy (668), which lacks the legacy parser/protocol/link logic; it does not invoke either actual joint validator.
findings.contract: SPEC B3 requires the eligible returned publication AND actual serialized final/manifest/candidate byte/hash/protocol agreement AND correct exit semantics at consumers; the task explicitly requires actual consumer tests and rejects a comment-only joint claim. Same-root atomic publishing is necessary but is not this validation.
findings.impact: The advertised shared private validator is not shared and does not perform its claimed disk/protocol verification. main can retain0/1 eligibility when a mandatory published file is unavailable or corrupted, and legacy can accept/remove a root with missing required helper or an errored evidence row. Pure54 tests cannot establish actual legacy rejection because their copy is a different function.
findings.minimal_fix: Implement one internal byte/protocol checker in an allowed existing module and have both real tool and legacy consumer invoke it; tests must invoke that actual checker. Read actual final/manifest/candidate (and required artifacts), validate full hashes/lengths, JSON shapes/mode/root/protocol, final links, all row errors, terminal/original cleanup/report qualification and mode-specific outcome. Parsing/read errors fail closed to unreliable3. Keep ordinary failed1 distinct from accepted expected fault. The CLI cannot observe its own future OS exit: the external recorder/acceptor must separately compare the real observed exit to that validated mode/result. Do not claim an in-memory exit field proves outer exit.
findings.direct_counterexample_design: Real temp FS + mocked supervisor: let the real publisher complete, then simulate one final/candidate/helper read EIO or corrupt/remove a record before invoking the actual validator; main/consumer must reject with3/no acceptance/no evidence deletion. Require valid normal0 and exact expected-fault1 controls; ordinary businessfailure1 and extra-error fault1 must reject acceptance. Feed valid byte hashes but invalid JSON protocol/link/mode and require rejection. Mutating the actual legacy checker must fail its consumer tests; currently modifying it cannot affect consumerAccepts tests. These are future guarded test designs, not executed here.
findings.fixed_subparts: publishEvidence:467-495 uses same-owned-root exclusive wx temp, full write, successful close, rename; catch:1630-1650 revokes returned kind/fault/authority/exit3 without overwriting a possibly complete final. The byte-backed test harness fixes mutable-reference evidence. Those improvements are accepted statically.
findings.runtime: NOT_RUN; no actual CLI/outer exit/kernel evidence granted

findings.title: The requested already-computed receipt digest strings remain absent
findings.reachable_precondition: Any accepted receipt/accumulator goes through diagnosticSnapshot and candidate/final persistence.
findings.actual_call_path: CacheReceiptAccumulator.state already computes copied events_digest/waits_digest/identities_digest; diagnosticSnapshot drops them from both receipt_summary and accumulator_summary. runPositivePilot persists only those reduced summaries. Report §6 supplies counts/flags and explicitly admits no digest strings, yet claims NOTE02 satisfied.
findings.contract: SPEC B4 and MAIN_COMBINED note require the already-computed bounded receipt digest/accumulator facts, not raw segments or R6 full replay.
findings.impact: No new cleanup or signal escape is established; saved minimal receipts cannot be compared by the requested existing digest values. Counts are honest but insufficient to close this specific note.
findings.minimal_fix: Copy bounded validated digest strings from the existing receipt and accumulator into the private readonly diagnostic summaries; persist them and report the actual computed values with evidence location. Retain raw_segments_saved=false and do not invent raw segments.
findings.direct_counterexample_design: Actual supervisor plus mocked protocol segment with known digests: assert diagnostic/candidate/final strings equal the accumulator/validated receipt values and survive repeated snapshot reads. Confirm report cites computed strings rather than only counts.
